saw_lines: People buy a dupe fragrance to smell like the designer bottle, then reorder the one that gets compliments.
So the sale is won in the first line, where a shopper decides whether the scent matches a designer bottle they know.
Your site shows 58,397 reviews, yet 0 of 30 ads use a review number. Print that count on the creative and open two ads with a customer quote.

ads.source: Meta Ad Library, active ads, 18 Oct 2026
points: Your site shows 58,397 reviews, yet 0 of 30 ads carry a review number, so buyers never see the proof before the click. Print 58,397 reviews on the creative and open two ads with a customer quote in the first line.
7 of your 26 copy ads open on the same “stop falling for luxury markups” line, and the rest use one-off openers. Test two new angles against it, one on the bundle offer and one on a review quote.
9 of your Shop now ads send buyers to the homepage, so a new visitor has to hunt for the scent the copy describes. Point each one to the exact dupe it names, like the gourmand or vanilla scent.
Your site promotes free shipping over $75, yet 0 of 26 ads mention it, so new buyers have no reason to act. Put free shipping over $75 in line one of new first buyer ads, and name fast NZ dispatch.

ads_1: Review-led creative opening on a customer quote, tested against the luxury markup hook
